```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Registers the site's Plotly template; colours live in site_utils/palette.py
from site_utils import palette, plotly_theme

# ---------------------------
# Import data and format
data = pd.read_csv("assets/eb_2023.csv").set_index("Flow")
df = data.loc[:, "Coal":].astype("float").reset_index()

# --------- Define fuels, and flows ---------------

fuels = ['Coal', 'Crude oil', 'Oil products', 'Natural gas', 'Nuclear', 'Hydro', 'Geo-therm., Solar etc.',
        'Biofuels and Waste', 'Electricity', 'Heat']
primary_flows = ['Production', 'Imports']
transformation_flows = ['Electricity plants', 'CHP plants', 'Heat plants',
                        'Blast furnaces', 'Gas works', 'Coke/pat. fuel/BKB/PB plants',
                        'Oil refineries', 'Petrochemical plants', 'Liquefaction plants',
                        'Other transformation', 
                        'Losses']
final_flows = ['INDUSTRY', 'TRANSPORT', 'OTHER', 'Energy industry own use','NON-ENERGY USE', 'Exports', 'Intl. marine bunkers', 
                 'Intl. aviation bunkers']



# --------- Define Colors ---------------

fuel_colors = palette.FUEL_COLORS
hex_to_rgba = palette.hex_to_rgba

def get_link_color(source, target):
    if source in fuel_colors:
        return hex_to_rgba(fuel_colors[source], 0.5)
    elif target in fuel_colors:
        return hex_to_rgba(fuel_colors[target], 0.5)
    else:
        return hex_to_rgba(palette.NEUTRAL, 0.3)

x_pos = {}
for n in primary_flows:
    x_pos[n] = 0.05           # far left
for n in fuels:
    x_pos[n] = 0.30           # mid-left
for n in transformation_flows:
    x_pos[n] = 0.60           # mid-right
for n in final_flows:
    x_pos[n] = 0.85           # far right
    
import numpy as np

y_pos = {}
def distribute_y(group, start=0.05, end=0.95):
    spacing = np.linspace(start, end, len(group))
    for n, y in zip(group, spacing):
        y_pos[n] = y

links = []


# Primary flows
for flow in primary_flows:
    for fuel in fuels:
        val = df.loc[df['Flow'] == flow, fuel].values[0]
        if val > 0:
            links.append((flow, fuel, abs(val)))
        if val < 0:
            links.append((fuel, flow, abs(val)))

# 2. Transformation flows


for flow in transformation_flows:
    for fuel in fuels:
        val = df.loc[df['Flow'] == flow, fuel].values[0]
        if val > 0:
            links.append((flow, fuel, abs(val)))
        if val < 0:
            links.append((fuel, flow, abs(val)))
            

# 3. Final flows
for flow in final_flows:
    for fuel in fuels:
        val = df.loc[df['Flow'] == flow, fuel].values[0]
        if val > 0:
            links.append((fuel, flow, abs(val)))
        if val < 0:
            links.append((fuel, flow, abs(val)))


# --- Optional filtering to declutter ---

link_colors = [get_link_color(s, t) for s, t, _ in links]
# total = sum([v for _, _, v in links])
# links = [(s, t, v) for s, t, v in links if v > 0.005 * total]

# nodes = list(dict.fromkeys(primary_flows + fuels + transformation_flows + final_flows))
nodes = primary_flows + fuels + transformation_flows + final_flows
used_nodes = set([s for s, _, _ in links] + [t for _, t, _ in links])
nodes = [n for n in nodes if n in used_nodes]
node_indices = {node: i for i, node in enumerate(nodes)}

sources, targets, values = zip(*links)

node_colors = []
for n in nodes:
    if n in fuel_colors:
        node_colors.append(fuel_colors[n])
    elif n in primary_flows:
        node_colors.append(palette.NODE_PRIMARY)
    elif n in transformation_flows:
        node_colors.append(palette.NODE_TRANSFORMATION)
    elif n in final_flows:
        node_colors.append(palette.NODE_FINAL)
    else:
        node_colors.append(palette.NEUTRAL)

distribute_y(primary_flows)
distribute_y(fuels)
distribute_y(transformation_flows)
distribute_y(final_flows)

fig = go.Figure(data=[go.Sankey(
    arrangement = 'snap',
    node=dict(
        pad=20,
        thickness=15,
        label=nodes,
        color= node_colors,
        x=[x_pos[n] for n in nodes],
        y=[y_pos[n] for n in nodes]
    ),
    link=dict(
        source=[node_indices[s] for s in sources],
        target=[node_indices[t] for t in targets],
        value=values,
        # color="rgba(0,150,250,0.4)"
        color=link_colors
    )
)])

# fig.update_layout(title_text="South Africa Energy Balance - 2023", font_size=10)
fig.update_layout(
    title_text="South Africa Energy Balance - 2023",
    # Text colour is supplied by the page's CSS so it follows the light/dark theme
    title=dict(x=0, font=dict(size=22)),
    font=dict(size=11),
    # font_size=11,
    annotations=[
        dict(
            text="<i>Source: Vuyo Mbam based on South Africa Energy Balance 2023 (IEA, DMRE)</i>",
            xref="paper", yref="paper",
            x=0, y=-0.12,          # position below chart
            showarrow=False,
            font=dict(size=10),
            xanchor='left',
        )
    ],
    margin=dict(t=60, b=80, l=5, r=10),
    height = 500,
    # width = 1000,
)


fig.show(config={'displayModeBar': False})

```

# Areas of Expertise
::: {.grid .expertise-section}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .expertise-card}
<!-- {{< fa chart-line >}} -->
{{< iconify mdi power-from-grid >}}

#### Techno-economic Analysis
Skilled in modelling energy yield performance of multiple energy technologies and discounted cashflow analysis (DCF) to investigate financial metrics such as the NPV, IRR, and payback period to inform investment decisions and policy recommendations.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .expertise-card}
{{< fa diagram-project >}}

#### Energy System Modelling
Long-term energy system planning using capacity mix projection models, including OSeMOSYS and bespoke tools, and power system dispatch modelling, with analysis of the resulting dispatch and system marginal prices.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .expertise-card}
{{< fa chart-line >}}

#### Macroeconomic Impact Modelling
Development of input-output models (multiplier-based) to model macroeconomic impacts (jobs, GDP, etc.) of in energy projects throughout their operational life. 
:::
:::

<script>
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
        // Fade experience and education cards in as they scroll into view.
        // (Without JavaScript, or with reduced motion, they are simply visible.)
        var items = document.querySelectorAll(".timeline-item, .edu-card");
        if (!("IntersectionObserver" in window)) {
            items.forEach(function (i) { i.classList.add("is-visible"); });
            return;
        }
        var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
            entries.forEach(function (entry) {
                if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                    entry.target.classList.add("is-visible");
                    observer.unobserve(entry.target);
                }
            });
        }, { threshold: 0.15 });
        items.forEach(function (i) { observer.observe(i); });
    });
</script>
```

# More about Me

I am an energy sector analyst and advisor at Kuungana Advisory Limited, where I lead workstreams on energy system modelling for South Africa and other countries in the Southern African Power Pool (SAPP). I combine technical and financial modelling to turn complex analysis into clear insights that inform transactions, route-to-market strategies and investment decisions for project developers, power traders, utilities and financial institutions. I also contribute to energy policy and regulation projects in SAPP member countries and beyond, mostly in low- and middle-income countries.

Previously, I was an energy economist at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), where my projects included:

- a Clean Cooking Roadmap for Mpumalanga province
- an Offshore Wind Roadmap for South Africa
- an analysis of localisation opportunities in the solar PV and battery energy storage value chains
- an assessment of how ready South Africa's education and training ecosystem is for a green hydrogen economy

      <div class="g-col-12 g-col-md-6">
        <label for="cf-org" class="form-label">Organisation <span class="contact-optional">(optional)</span></label>
        <input id="cf-org" name="organisation" class="form-control" autocomplete="organization">
      </div>
      <div class="g-col-12 g-col-md-6">
        <label for="cf-topic" class="form-label">I am getting in touch about</label>
        <select id="cf-topic" name="topic" class="form-select">
          <option>A job opportunity</option>
          <option>Requesting your CV</option>
          <option>Consulting or collaboration</option>
          <option>Speaking or an interview</option>
          <option>Something else</option>
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="g-col-12">

        <textarea id="cf-message" name="message" rows="6" class="form-control" required></textarea>
      </div>
      <div class="g-col-12 contact-actions">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-success btn-lg">Send message</button>
        <span id="cf-status" class="contact-status" role="status" aria-live="polite"></span>
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="contact-note">Your message is sent to me through Web3Forms, a form-relay service. I will only use your details to reply.</p>
  </form>
  <p class="contact-fallback">Prefer email? Write to <a id="cf-mail" href="#">vuyombam69 [at] gmail [dot] com</a></p>
</div>
<script>
    // The address is assembled here so it never appears in the page source for scrapers.
    const CONTACT_EMAIL = ["vuyombam69", "gmail.com"].join("@");

    function initContactForm(form) {
        const key = form.dataset.accessKey;
        if (!key || key.startsWith("PASTE")) return;      // not configured: keep the form hidden
        form.hidden = false;
        form.querySelector('[name="access_key"]').value = key;

        const status = document.getElementById("cf-status");
        const button = form.querySelector('button[type="submit"]');
        const say = (msg) => { status.textContent = msg; };

        form.addEventListener("submit", async function (event) {
            event.preventDefault();
            const data = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form));
            data.subject = "Website enquiry: " + data.topic + " (" + data.name + ")";
            button.disabled = true;
            say("Sending...");
            try {
                const response = await fetch(form.action, {
                    method: "POST",
                    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json" },
                    body: JSON.stringify(data)
                });
                const result = await response.json();
                if (!response.ok || !result.success) throw new Error(result.message || "Request failed");
                form.reset();
                say("Sent. Thank you, I will get back to you soon.");
            } catch (error) {
                say("Not sent. Please email me directly at " + CONTACT_EMAIL + ".");
            } finally {
                button.disabled = false;
            }
        });
    }

    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
        const mail = document.getElementById("cf-mail");
        mail.href = "mailto:" + CONTACT_EMAIL;
        mail.textContent = CONTACT_EMAIL;
        initContactForm(document.getElementById("contact-form"));
    });
</script>
```
